sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Adesh Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Adesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A.
for the State and also perused the record.
2.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case
Crime No. 72 of 2019, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 506 of Ipc, Police Station Khekra,
District Baghpat, with a prayer to enlarge her on anticipatory bail.

3.  As per prosecution story, in all Rs.8 lakhs are stated to have taken by the husband of the applicant Naim Ansar from the informant on the pretext that he shall get him a visa issued for travelling to Kuwait.
When the informant went to the house of the applicant, the applicant and her brother-in-law Imran are stated to have scuffed him away from their house after threatening him.
It is also alleged that the ticket and visa given to the informant by the husband of the applicant were found fake.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that she is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case owing to her relationship with the main accused Naim Ansar, who is her husband.
She has apprehension of her arrest.
She has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned counsel has further stated that no amount has been transferred to the account of the applicant.

The amount transferred, if any, is to the account of her husband Naim Ansar i.e.
Rs.1,80,000/-.
She is just a housewife and has nothing to do with the said offence.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against her.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, she will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history to her credit.

7. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may be adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
